completed: Observed merge-history workflow commit dd1aea669cafbed484738dc8274bfa4d6adaacec failed both dedicated and integrated CI rather than assuming green.
Isolated a faulty retired-identity merge regression fixture: it expected rejection when the selected identity was still active in one parent and therefore not actually retired.
Corrected the regression fixture in 5ee5f132226866fe8f0344b6cb005c85d5d14562 so the reused identity is genuinely present in a parent retirement history.
Audited timestamp representation equality and found raw string comparison could treat Z, +00:00, or equivalent offsets as different records/repins despite denoting the same instant.

Normalized provenance timestamp comparison to UTC instant semantics in 9716099e7ab9f136a570e42a725463f96197c7b2 and added regressions for equivalent encodings in 89ce5d01beb286f741aff9a575387d58f6612981.
checkpoint.observation: The prior merge regression failure was a test-model error, not evidence that valid merge reconciliation should be abandoned. Timestamp identity is now semantic by instant rather than raw textual encoding. CI for the latest regression commit was queued at checkpoint time and is not yet claimed green.
checkpoint.next_action: Verify dedicated and integrated CI for 89ce5d01beb286f741aff9a575387d58f6612981. If green, audit whether provenance-history complexity still provides net protection relative to its maintenance/CI cost; simplify or retire rules that no longer serve the program's utilization and integrity goals.
